note: Buildings, building slots and construction money. Costs, slots and effects are gameplay values. Construction points come from civilian factories; money is paid from the budget as the work progresses, scaled by the country's price level (GDP per person against the reference), and counts against the public investment the 2000 budgets already contain (investment_allowance_pct_gdp). Starting factories are derived from World Bank 2000 industry value added (economy.json factory_value_bn) and placed on provinces by population and infrastructure; starting refineries follow 2000 oil rents.

buildings.name: Infrastructure
buildings.description: Roads, rail and utilities in a province: better supply, movement and growth, and room for more buildings.

buildings.name: Civilian factory
buildings.description: Industrial capacity: builds construction projects, and makes consumer and industrial goods when it is not building.

buildings.name: Military factory
buildings.description: Capacity for military equipment, assigned to production lines in the Production tab.

buildings.name: Oil refinery
buildings.description: Turns crude oil into fuel for the home market and for export. Needs oil production.

buildings.name: Renewable power plant
buildings.description: Wind or solar parks with grid connections: cheaper, cleaner power.

buildings.name: Data centre
buildings.description: Large computing centres for business, government and research.

buildings.name: Air base
buildings.description: Runways, shelters and fuel for combat aircraft: a stronger air force over the front.

buildings.name: Port
buildings.description: Container terminals and docks: cheaper trade. Coastal provinces only.
